conformetry-generators.description: Reconciles generated code against the conformetry templates it was scaffolded from. `check` runs on a pull request, because drift is the author's to fix in the same change; `write` runs on the default branch's release, alongside every other derivation. Named on its own by whichever caller wants it — `configuration/lint-staged.config.ts`, the Lint Codebase workflow, and the release workflow — rather than through a shared aggregate, the way `codebase:codometer` and `codebase:callidescope` are named by their own callers.

conventional-config.description: Reconciles derived conventional-commit configuration against `configuration/conventional.config.cjs`. `check` runs on a pull request; `write` runs on the default branch's release.

devcontainer-configuration.description: Reconciles the cloud devcontainer configuration's synced fields against the local one. `check` runs on a pull request; `write` runs on the default branch's release.

issue-labels.description: Adds the type and scope labels a submitted `issue.yml` body implies. Its destination is GitHub itself rather than a file, so reaching it needs a token that neither a fork nor a developer's `lint-code` run has: the 🦹 Continuous Compliance workflow runs it directly through node rather than through this Nx target on an issue's `opened` event, and nothing else names it. This target exists for a human running it locally with their own credentials.

package-manifests.description: Reconciles derived package manifest metadata (author, license, repository, homepage, bugs) across all 29 publishable packages against root package.json and project paths. `check` runs on pull requests; `write` runs on release.

pull-request-labels.description: Reconciles this repository's GitHub label vocabulary against `configuration/conventional.config.cjs`. Its destination is GitHub itself rather than a file, so reaching it needs a token that neither a fork nor a developer's `lint-code` run has: the pull request workflow that holds one runs `write` directly through node rather than through this Nx target on `opened`/`reopened`, and nothing else names it. This target exists for a human running it locally with their own credentials.

pull-request-template.description: Reconciles derived pull request template content. `check` runs on a pull request; `write` runs on the default branch's release.

skill-exclusions.description: Reconciles the installed-skill exclusion lists against `skills-lock.json`. `check` runs on a pull request; `write` runs on the default branch's release.

start.description: Runs every synchronization command in one process — the only target that does. Not referenced by CI: no workflow or `configuration/lint-staged.config.ts` pattern names `start`, so this exists purely for a human at a terminal who wants to check or write everything in one command, uncached because nothing should ever depend on its result. Each synchronization also runs on its own through its own Nx target — for example `nx run synchronization:skill-exclusions:check` — which is what every other caller uses.
